title: Pin-event eval orchestrator with deterministic impact scoring
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build an orchestrator service that runs automated evaluation suites when a model version pin or catalog upgrade is committed. The service must produce a deterministic numeric impact score per pin event (global and per-customer), attach evidence (sampled inputs & outputs, key metrics), and emit a decision token used by rollout controllers to allow/hold/rollback upgrades.
acceptance_criteria: Orchestrator receives pin events from catalog and customer-pin API and enqueues evaluation jobs within 30s
Impact score computed deterministically from weighted metric deltas (latency, token-cost, top-level quality metric) and a configurable customer-priority multiplier
Decision token produced with 'allow' | 'hold' | 'rollback-suggested' and persisted to audit log
Canary sampling controller can read decision token and gate a canary rollout automatically
Evidence bundles (top 100 diffing examples + summary metrics) are stored in S3 and linked from the decision token
End-to-end integration tests and a synthetic smoke test succeed in CI with mocked pin events
implementation_notes: Reuse existing eval runner (ENG-2411) for executing suites; add a lightweight orchestration layer to sequence smoke -> regression -> benchmark steps
Impact score formula: normalized delta across configured metrics; default weights: quality 0.6, latency 0.2, cost 0.2; allow project-level overrides
Deterministic sampling: use event hash + seed to select 1k examples per customer for fair comparisons
Budgeting: jobs must respect a per-event compute budget (default 10 GPU-minutes); fall back to prioritized test subset when budget hits
Implement a 'fast-fail' safety path: if quality delta > threshold, mark 'rollback-suggested' immediately and surface urgent alert
Store decision tokens in audit-indexed DB table with immutability guarantees and link to console for operator review
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged rollout: start with internal orgs only
Week 1: run in dry-run mode (decision tokens created but not enforced), collect false positives/negatives
Week 2: enable enforcement for non-critical catalog upgrades (low traffic models)
Week 3: expand to customer-pinned models for orgs that opt in; monitor SLA/quality
Full launch after 3 operational weeks and sign-off from SRE and PM
test_plan: Unit tests for scoring math and deterministic sampling
Integration tests with eval-runner and S3 artifact store in CI
Synthetic smoke pipeline: push synthetic pin event -> run orchestrator -> verify decision token and artifacts
Load test: simulate 200 pin events/hour to validate queuing and budget enforcement
Post-launch: daily regression checks against baseline for 2 weeks
